evals.prompt: /team-review 482 — this PR touches our payment processing and adds a new auth middleware, want a thorough review before we merge
assertions: Ingests the PR via gh pr view/gh pr diff (or equivalent) rather than guessing at the changes
Runs a Phase 1 project discovery step before spawning reviewers
Given security-sensitive scope (payments, auth), selects full mode (7 reviewers) or clearly justifies why not
Spawns a security reviewer and an adversary reviewer that challenges the other reviewers' findings
Produces a single consolidated report with severity-classified findings (Critical/Major/Minor/Nit) rather than raw per-agent dumps
Does not edit any code or commit changes

evals.prompt: /team-review 119 --lite just want a quick sanity check, keep it cheap
assertions: Honors the --lite flag by using Task subagents instead of the Teammate API
Spawns the reduced 4-agent lite-mode team rather than the full 7-agent team
Still includes an adversary-style pass that challenges/cross-checks the other findings
Generates a report with file:line findings and severity levels
Does not modify code or run the test suite

evals.prompt: we just merged a big schema migration in commit 9f3ab21, can you get the team to review it for architectural issues, focus on architecture only
assertions: Detects the commit SHA input and ingests it via git show / git diff-tree (or equivalent) rather than treating it as a PR number
Honors --focus architecture by spawning only arch-reviewer and adversary-reviewer, not the full 7-agent roster
Adversary reviewer waits for and challenges the architecture reviewer's findings rather than running independently first
Final report is scoped to architectural findings (data modeling, API contracts, schema/pattern concerns)
Does not attempt to fix or refactor the schema itself
